newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait MP undergoes surgery after killing bid.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait MP undergoes surgery after killing bid.

text.p: A leading Kuwaiti opposition parliamentarian, Abdullah al-Naibari, was shot twice in an assassination attempt on Friday and a family member said he was in a stable condition prior to undergoing surgery.
"Thanks be to God, he is not in a life-threatening situation," Naibari's younger brother, sea captain Abul-Rahman, told Reuters as doctors operated on the MP's jaw.

Naibari, 61, was rushed to hospital with bullet wounds in his jaw and shoulder after gunmen opened fire at his car as he drove home in Kuwait City from a beachhouse close to the southern border with Saudi Arabia.
The MP's wife, Feryal al-Furaih, who was also in the car, suffered a slight shoulder wound and was doing well, Abdul-Rahman al-Naibari said.
Fellow MP Sami al-Munayes, when asked if the attack was politically motivated, said: "What happened can only be explained in the context of that."

"It is a battle between right and wrong and defending the people's rights," he said. Munayes urged the government "to strike with an iron fist, with deeds and not words," all forms of "corruption" in the country.
Munayes expressed hope that Naibari would return to parliament to resume combating "public funds' abusers".
An Interior Ministry spokesman vowed swift action to arrest the assailants. Police sources said two vehicles were involved in the attempt.
Political sources said the authorities were currently debriefing an eyewitness who had rushed Naibari and his wife to the Adan Hospital, south of Kuwait City.
There was no immediate information about who was behind the attack.
But, politcial sources strongly hinted that Naibari's frequent questions in parliament on what they called "stealing of public funds" and arms deals had created many enemies.
Naibari, a pro-democracy vetran, played a key role in 1992 parliamentary efforts to combat what MPs described as graft and mismanagement of state funds.
The acting prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah, said the attack was directed "against the Kuwaiti people and Kuwait" and was meant to trigger a "strife".
Parliament Speaker Ahmad al-Saadoun told journalists at the hospital where Naibari received treatment that "corrupt elements" were behind the attack.
In a similar incident, former MP Hamad al-Jouan was crippled in an assassination attempt in 1991 weeks after Kuwait's liberation from a seven-month Iraqi occupation.
Jouan and Naibari were members of parliament when it was dissolved in 1986. Both were of the most prominent campaigners for the restoration of democracy that was achieved in 1992.
Political assassinations are rare in the Gulf state.
Diplomats say some residents held unlicenced weapons they kept since the 1991 Gulf War despite efforts by the state to collect the weapons left behind by fleeing Iraqi troops.
